items.grounds: Re-derived both ways from the staged bytes. The row's close-seam ground as written is the construction contrast named in device_notes ('the signal that does is the shift in construction'); no ruled tier-1 class is named at oshb:Isa.40.17|40.18, and observed_substrate_signals carries only oracle_frame.topic_onset. Bytes: the span is unaddressed third person throughout -- מִֽי מָדַ֨ד (oshb:Isa.40.12, tier: byte), מִֽי תִכֵּ֥ן (oshb:Isa.40.13, tier: byte), אֶת מִ֤י נוֹעָץ֙ (oshb:Isa.40.14, tier: byte), closing נֶחְשְׁבוּ לֽוֹ (oshb:Isa.40.17, tier: byte), with no second-person form anywhere in oshb:Isa.40.12-40.17 (each verse read in full against both witnesses' renderings; the extract stages no morphology layer, so this is a pointed-bytes-plus-rendering claim) -- and the next verse opens a second-person-plural address, תְּדַמְּי֣וּן and תַּ֥עַרְכוּ (oshb:Isa.40.18, tier: byte, each against its own verse; web:Isa.40.18 renders both as 'you'), an address absent from the whole span and continuing at oshb:Isa.40.21 and 40.25. That is the ruled addressee/scene-shift class, present at the seam and unused. Mark inventory re-read at MT keys: SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.40.11, 40.16 and 40.24 exactly as the row states, nothing at oshb:Isa.40.17 (absence is not counterevidence; it only confirms the construction contrast stands alone as the named ground). Tested against the row: the boundary itself is byte-sound, since the tier-1 onset at 40.18 supports the same cut, so the defect is a defective warrant rather than a load-bearing one -- medium as filed. This is the same seam as the onset finding on the following row; one seam-pair edit cures both. Not a span item.

Re-collated at every tier. The row's sentence 'not a recurrence in the Hebrew at any tier' is byte-false at the particle level: הֲל֤וֹא (oshb:Isa.40.21, tier: byte) collates against oshb:Isa.40.28 at accent_stripped tier, and הֲל֨וֹא (oshb:Isa.40.28, tier: byte) collates against oshb:Isa.40.21 at accent_stripped tier, the two tokens differing only in cantillation. The fourfold pattern is in the Hebrew bytes, not in the rendering: הֲל֤וֹא, הֲל֣וֹא, הֲל֛וֹא, הֲלוֹא֙ (oshb:Isa.40.21, tier: byte, each against its own verse) -- four tokens of the one particle -- and the two verb roots recur in the same order across the seam, תֵֽדְעוּ֙ then תִשְׁמָ֔עוּ (oshb:Isa.40.21, tier: byte) against יָדַ֜עְתָּ then שָׁמַ֗עְתָּ (oshb:Isa.40.28, tier: byte), each against its own verse, in different persons and stems, so no contiguous-skeleton match between the pairs. The clause-level comparison is honestly tier NONE in both directions -- הֲל֤וֹא תֵֽדְעוּ֙ against oshb:Isa.40.28 and הֲל֨וֹא יָדַ֜עְתָּ אִם לֹ֣א שָׁמַ֗עְתָּ against oshb:Isa.40.21 both return none -- which is exactly what the following row states, clause against clause; this row's unqualified 'at any tier' and its 'rendering-level echo' label are the form the bytes refuse, and the negative names no count object. The device straddles the row's own close seam (oshb:Isa.40.21 inside, 40.28 outside), so the tier misstatement lands on a cross-seam cohesion disclosure; it does not disturb the boundary, which the imperative onset at oshb:Isa.40.26 and the envelope closure at 40.25 carry. Defective tier claim, not load-bearing: medium as filed. Not a span item.

Re-derived from the bytes and from the ruled strategy text. The operative-category law sits under the unit_type vocabulary ('each line above names the operative category, not an exclusive grant; any closed-vocabulary value applies wherever the row's own bytes carry that form, with a one-sentence deviation disclosure'); it governs which closed-vocabulary unit_type value a row may carry, not which signal class may carry a seam, so the device_notes appeal ('disclosed here per the operative-category allowance since no woe, massa, or divine-speech-frame formula opens or closes this span') does not license the construction as a boundary driver. Even read charitably as a salvation_oracle deviation disclosure, the same sentence expressly disclaims 'an imperative or addressee shift' as the boundary ground, and that disclaimed class stands in the onset verse's own bytes: the preceding material is unaddressed third person through נֶחְשְׁבוּ לֽוֹ (oshb:Isa.40.17, tier: byte), and the onset opens a second-person-plural address, תְּדַמְּי֣וּן and תַּ֥עַרְכוּ (oshb:Isa.40.18, tier: byte, each against its own verse; web:Isa.40.18 'will you liken', 'will you compare'), continuing at oshb:Isa.40.21 and 40.25. The envelope the row argues is honest at its stated tiers -- וְאֶל מִ֖י (oshb:Isa.40.18, tier: byte) collates against oshb:Isa.40.25 at accent_stripped tier, while the fuller clauses וְאֶל מִ֖י תְּדַמְּי֣וּן (oshb:Isa.40.18, tier: byte) and וְאֶל מִ֥י תְדַמְּי֖וּנִי (oshb:Isa.40.25, tier: byte) return none against each other in both directions -- so it is a matching two-word interrogative prefix, not a byte-identical refrain that the refrain-close law would let carry the seam by itself. observed_substrate_signals carries topic_onset, inclusio_bracket and postpositive_inquit, no addressee_shift. Boundary byte-sound; warrant grounded on a non-ruled class with a misapplied law citation: medium as filed. Same seam as the close finding on the preceding row; one seam-pair edit cures both. Not a span item.

Re-derived from the bytes and the mark inventory. The close as written: the only ground named at oshb:Isa.41.16|41.17 in boundary_rationale is 'sealed by a PE parashah mark (single-witness), backing the division there'; strongest_rejected_alternative argues only why the fear-not chain runs past 41.13 (an internal-cohesion point) and then calls both marks 'not as the deciding ground', which leaves no deciding ground named at all. The mark is real (inventory at MT keys: PE at 41:16, SAMEKH at 41:7 and 41:13, PE at 41:20, nothing at 41:17), but Prophets parashah is tier-3 weak corroboration, never a driver. oshb:Isa.41.17 appears in no field of the row (checked against boundary_rationale, strongest_rejected_alternative, device_notes and all fourteen boundary_evidence_refs). The unnamed tier-1 ground is byte-present: the span is second person throughout -- וְאַתָּה֙ ... בְּחַרְתִּ֑יךָ (oshb:Isa.41.8, tier: byte, each against its own verse), אַל תִּירָא֙ (oshb:Isa.41.10, tier: byte), וְאַתָּה֙ תָּגִ֣יל (oshb:Isa.41.16, tier: byte) -- while oshb:Isa.41.17-41.20 carry no second-person form (first-person promises and third-person referents, read verse by verse against both witnesses; no morphology layer is staged, so this is a pointed-bytes-plus-rendering claim), so the addressee is dropped exactly at the close. The cross-seam title recurrence is also byte-true: קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Isa.41.14, tier: byte) collates against oshb:Isa.41.16 and against oshb:Isa.41.20 at skeleton tier (the 41.14 token carries meteg, retained at accent_stripped, so skeleton is the honest tier), בִּקְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (oshb:Isa.41.16, tier: byte) against oshb:Isa.41.20 returns none, and the bare core קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (oshb:Isa.43.3, tier: byte) collates against both oshb:Isa.41.16 and 41.20 at byte tier; the row lists the three sites with tiers but never states that the recurrence into 41.20 leaves its close undisturbed, the sentence the following row does carry for the same pair. Boundary byte-sound on the addressee drop; the defect is the warrant (a tier-3 mark in the driver role) plus a disclosure gap: medium as filed. Not a span item.

Re-derived from the onset verse's own bytes. Every reference to the pair is third person: הָעֲנִיִּ֨ים וְהָאֶבְיוֹנִ֜ים מְבַקְשִׁ֥ים (oshb:Isa.41.17, tier: byte; plural participle subject), then לְשׁוֹנָ֖ם, אֶעֱנֵ֔ם and אֶעֶזְבֵֽם (oshb:Isa.41.17, tier: byte, each against its own verse; third-person-plural suffixes on a noun and on two first-person verbs), rendered 'their tongue', 'answer them', 'forsake them' at web:Isa.41.17. Read verse by verse, oshb:Isa.41.17-41.20 carries no second-person form (first-person verbs at 41.18-41.19, a third-person purpose clause at 41.20; both witnesses agree; no morphology layer is staged), whereas the preceding unit is second person from וְאַתָּה֙ (oshb:Isa.41.8, tier: byte) to וְאַתָּה֙ תָּגִ֣יל (oshb:Isa.41.16, tier: byte). So 'addressed to the same unnamed poor and needy without renaming the addressee' (boundary_rationale) and 'without renaming the addressee' (strongest_rejected_alternative) are byte-false form claims: the pair is a described referent, not an addressee, and the second-person addressee of the preceding unit is dropped at this seam rather than carried across. The divine-title clause in the same sentence is byte-true (אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל, oshb:Isa.41.17, tier: byte). Load-bearing test: the row's cut rests on the topic onset plus the PE mark (inventory re-read: PE at MT 41:16 and 41:20, nothing at 41:17); the false clause argues continuity against the row's own cut rather than carrying it, and the boundary is byte-sound on the very addressee drop the row misdescribes. Byte-false form claim inside the warrant, not alone load-bearing: medium as filed. Not a span item.

Re-derived both ways. The onset as written rests on a content characterisation ('a third-person divine presentation of an unnamed servant figure') plus the PE mark at MT 41:29 (inventory re-read: PE at 41:29 and 42:4; tier-3, never a driver), with no ruled frame class named; the close is tier-1 and exact -- כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר הָאֵ֣ל יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Isa.42.5, tier: byte) -- and the koh-amar skeleton sweep over chs 41-43 returns exactly oshb:Isa.42.5, 43.1, 43.14 and 43.16 (sweep: 4 verses, none in ch 41, none of the four royal-messenger sites), so the digit holds. Under the ruled vocabulary the servant_song value applies only where the unit's bounds are argued from tier-1 seams, which the onset side does not do: the defect is real and medium as filed (the boundary is not byte-shown wrong, and the row already holds it at low confidence with the frontier flag set). One correction to the finding's grounds, which the remediation docket must carry: the trial speech's second-person-plural address is real -- רִֽיבְכֶ֖ם (oshb:Isa.41.21, tier: byte), הֵן אַתֶּ֣ם מֵאַ֔יִן (oshb:Isa.41.24, tier: byte), אִמְרֵיכֶֽם (oshb:Isa.41.26, tier: byte) -- but it is not dropped at oshb:Isa.42.1: its last form is that 41.26 suffix, and oshb:Isa.41.27-41.29 already carry no second-person form (first-person verbs at 41.27-41.28; third-person plural מַעֲשֵׂיהֶ֑ם and נִסְכֵּיהֶֽם at oshb:Isa.41.29, tier: byte, each against its own verse; read against both witnesses, no morphology layer staged). What the seam itself carries in the bytes is a presentative onset of a new referent -- הֵ֣ן כֻּלָּ֔ם (oshb:Isa.41.29, tier: byte) answered by הֵ֤ן עַבְדִּי֙ (oshb:Isa.42.1, tier: byte), the two particles collating at accent_stripped tier -- a referent/scene shift inside one continuing divine speech, not an addressee drop; the proposed field repair must be re-cut to name that shift, with the PE mark as corroboration, and the docket must judge whether it qualifies as a ruled scene shift explicit in the bytes. Residual, flagged not ruled: with no addressee change at 41.29|42.1, the tier-1-bounded speech from the summons at oshb:Isa.41.21 to the frame at 42.5 is a byte-grounded rival grouping that the neighbouring row dismisses as texture; that is a local seam question, not a book-level one, and this item carries no span proposal. Not a span item.
